Postgraduate Physics
Develop an in-depth understanding of energy and matter with postgraduate study in Physics.
Overview
Qualifications
People
Build your understanding of the fundamental nature of the universe and take the chance to apply your insights across a broad range of disciplines.
Studying in the School of Chemical and Physical Sciences, you'll get the benefit of strong cross-discipline links, unique research connections, and a collaborative approach.
You might take advantage of the School's strength in materials science and nanotechnology, where a combined expertise in both chemistry and physics gives it an edge. Or you might choose to work in areas where physics meets the earth sciences, engineering, or biology.
You can focus on theory or look into practical applications of your work, using the School's state-of-the-art research equipment and modern laboratory facilities.

Full story
Collaborate for success
The School's links with Wellington research institutes put you at the heart of the capital’s vibrant science scene. These include the MacDiarmid Institute for Advanced Materials and Nanotechnology and the Malaghan Institute of Medical Research on campus, and Paihau—Robinson Research Institute, Callaghan Innovation, GNS Science and the National Institute of Water and Atmospheric Research nearby. You might have your research project co-supervised by scientists from these institutes and benefit from their expertise and facilities.
Strong links with a wide range of technology companies, such as New Zealand Pharmaceuticals, Toshiba and Magritek, mean the results of your research can be picked up by industry.
Get the benefit of the international expertise and connections that come from the School's numerous research collaborations with leading universities and laboratories in the USA, Europe and Asia, many involving exchange visits of staff and students.
Leading researchers
Work with staff and researchers who are recognised internationally and publish regularly in peer-reviewed journals. Learn from their experience and expertise, and become a specialist in the field of physics.
Research topics
If you're thinking of doing a research project you can check the academic staff list to see the research interests of staff.
Topics include:
Electronic properties of materials
Interaction of light with condensed matter systems
Flow, diffusion and dispersion in porous media
Physics of soft materials
NMR method and equipment development
Radiation sensitive materials
Sensors and instrumentation
Theory of quantum transport in nanostructures
Computational materials modelling science and technology
Environmental physics
Astrophysics—radio and optical astronomy
Geomagnetism and paleomagnetism
Research
Careers
If you want to work as a physicist, a postgraduate degree is crucial in a range of different fields. You might work in new-product development, food processing, medical physics, patent law, research, or teaching.
Join the University's Physics graduates working for technology companies, government laboratories, and in related fields such as environmental or earth science.
Community
Postgraduate study at Victoria University of Wellington will help you build valuable relationships and networks with peers, university staff, and future colleagues.
You'll join the tight-knit Physics team, working closely alongside staff and getting the benefit of their expertise, advice, and support.
Along with state-of-the-art facilities, you'll get access to postgraduate workspaces.
Take opportunities to attend events and social functions and present to seminars. You'll also be encouraged to attend and participate in national and international conferences.
The Postgraduate Students' Association can give you information on study at the University and provides a voice for you on campus.
Live and study in the creative and scientific capital of New Zealand. As well as hosting the country's largest scientific community, Wellington offers a myriad of cultural and recreational opportunities. Compact and easy to get around, it's a great place to live and study.
